definition: Dynamic Prompt Construction is a core concept in Prompt Engineering. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What Dynamic Prompt Construction is
theory.body: Dynamic Prompt Construction describes the methods and patterns used within Prompt Engineering to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Dynamic Prompt Construction is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Dynamic Prompt Construction matters
theory.body: Without Dynamic Prompt Construction, systems built with Prompt Engineering are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Dynamic Prompt Construction works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Dynamic Prompt Construction follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Dynamic Prompt Construction.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Dynamic Prompt Construction
theory.body: Dynamic Prompt Construction offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
